preconditions.description: The number of towns n is between 3 and 10^5 inclusive.
The number of monasteries m is at least 2 and strictly less than n.

preconditions.expression: len(monastery_towns) == m and all(1 <= t <= n for t in monastery_towns) and len(set(monastery_towns)) == m
preconditions.description: The list of monastery towns contains exactly m distinct integers within the valid town index range.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v and 1 <= w <= 1000 for u, v, w in edges)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n-1 edges, each connecting two distinct valid towns with a positive integer weight.
The graph formed by the towns and edges is a connected tree (n nodes, n-1 edges, connected).

postconditions.description: The output consists of two integers separated by whitespace: the maximum number of unhappy pilgrims and the count of valid towns to destroy.
The first output integer equals the maximum number of pilgrims that can be made unhappy by destroying exactly one non-monastery town.

postconditions.expression: count_ways == count_optimal_towns(n, m, monastery_towns, edges, max_unhappy)
postconditions.description: The second output integer equals the number of non-monastery towns whose destruction results in exactly max_unhappy pilgrims becoming unhappy.
